data-fixed: MP tasks re-targeted for the soft Dex3 hand gains, failed replays removed
result.message:
The 5 MP tasks (g1_wholebody) replayed 4/100 (TabletopHandoverMP) after the Dex3 hand PD change (kp 40-80 -> 5/2.5, index/middle torque 0.7). Changes:

- Hand actions boosted: a' = a + (kp_old/kp_new - 1) * deadband(a - q_next), clipped to joint limits; only stall errors pushing away from the open pose (not releases). BendPickAndPlaceOnSofaMP: no boost on thumb_0 or the left hand. Settings per task in handboost.json.
- PickAndBendPlaceMP: 14-frame right-hand release appended to 10 episodes whose recording ended with the hand closed.
- PickAndBendPlaceMP, BendPickAndPlaceOnSofaMP: 20 frames holding the final row appended to every episode (released box lands inside the episode).
- Episodes failing the MuJoCo replay removed, rest renumbered: TabletopHandoverMP 76/100, BendPickMP 91/100, TabletopGraspMP 98/100, PickAndBendPlaceMP 49/57, BendPickAndPlaceOnSofaMP 75/99. stats.json / stats_psi0.json are those of the full datasets.

PickAndBendPlaceMP 49/49 and BendPickAndPlaceOnSofaMP 75/75 re-verified with a default replay after the hold frames.

result.title: data-fixed: fix 1-frame lag in re-rendered G1WholebodyBendPickMP-v0 videos
result.message: Fix off-by-one in the previous re-render commit: the replay video starts with the reset frame, but dataset frame k shows the state after action k, so the videos were one frame behind the states/actions. Now uses render frames [1, 1+length): frame-difference correlation with the original videos peaks at shift 0 for 100/100 episodes (was +1). Only videos change; codec, resolution, fps, frame counts and timestamps unchanged.

result.title: data-fixed: re-render G1WholebodyBendPickMP-v0 videos with per-episode table materials
result.message: Egocentric videos of all 100 episodes re-rendered with the current renderer so the table/ground materials match each episode's environment_config (as in eval). 100/100 replays succeeded. States, actions, meta and all non-video files are byte-identical; videos keep the same codec (h264 High, yuv420p), 640x360, 50 fps, frame counts and timestamps.
